newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch club Den Haag eyes stocks flotation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch club Den Haag eyes stocks flotation.

text.p: Dutch second division soccer side HFC ADO Den Haag said on Wednesday it was looking at the possibility of listing its shares on the New Market of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
To do so the club, based in The Hague, would set up a new unit called NV ADO Den Haag.

"This company ... aims at supplying the necessary financial means to the soccer club so it could return to the (Dutch) premier league and eventually to playing European soccer," the club said in a statement.
ADO Den Haag played a prominent role in Dutch and European soccer in the 1970s but later was relegated and fell back to a rather unspectacular position.
It is seventh in the Dutch second division, with one round to play. But it has also qualified for the play-offs through which it might secure promotion to the premier league in the 1997/98 season.
The club said a sound financial basis was a top priority given the hefty budgets which soccer clubs need to meet such expenses as accommodation and high player salaries.
When NV ADO Den Haag lists on the Amsterdam bourse, it wants shareholders' equity to be 15 million guilders ($7.8 million), it added.
ADO Den Haag previously said it planned a private share issue worth 10 million guilders as a prelude to a market listing within five years.
PSV Eindhoven, which won the Dutch premier league title last Sunday, said earlier this year it expected to be publicly quoted by the year 2005.
